title: Mechanically translated — 107 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit and how they are bound
description:
Mechanically translated — 107 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit, one Lean namespace, wing the machine. 107 close by exhaustion over a finite domain (by decide). Every one is sealed live in the append-only ledger.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used in this deposit's honest sense: correlation by derivation, not quantum entanglement, and no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 2 definition(s) are used by two or more theorems, binding 65 pair(s); the theorems fall into 93 strand(s), the largest of 11. Most binding: DR (11), M9 (5). 88 theorem(s) name no definition of the file and stand on their own statement.

2 · Imports. Built on: address.lean. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 3 file(s): src/proof/mechanical.lean, src/proof/address.lean, src/proof/fnv.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 107 sealed receipts fold to dcd36e87-128c-8d3b-8505-0cf4c78ba141. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed on this run. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (0, 5, 4, 3, 3, 6, 4). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs observed among each theorem's seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: priorart.lean (18 observed, 10.68 expected, lift 1.68), address.lean (32 observed, 20.18 expected, lift 1.59), fnv.lean (20 observed, 14.24 expected, lift 1.4). A lift near 1 is what chance gives. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 15.51; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.5. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). Chance, measured: over 200 reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to (seeded, so every rebuild gives the same numbers), a best lift at least this high arose in 63.0% of them — consistent with chance.

Prior art. the Boolean rows are De Morgan's laws — Augustus De Morgan, 1847 — written in the arithmetic of {0,1}; the group rows are the additive group of Z/9. Both long prior. No novelty is claimed here.
